standard_prerequisites.name: Pseudo-coherence is preserved by the derived pullback of complexes and the pull-push comparison
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the direct sum K^bullet oplus K^bullet[1] over R.

standard_prerequisites.name: A direct summand of a pseudo-coherent complex is pseudo-coherent

core_obligations: Record that the statement is a special case of the pushforward pseudo-coherence statement, and announce the second, independent argument (proof lines 21268-21270).
Use the exact sequence 0 -> R[x] -> R[x] -> R -> 0 to conclude that R is pseudo-coherent as an R[x]-module and hence obtain one implication from the pushforward statement (proof lines 21273-21276).

For the other implication, assume K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent over R[x] and use the pullback statement to conclude that K^bullet tensor^L_{R[x]} R is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules (proof lines 21277-21281).
Use the pull-push statement to conclude that K^bullet oplus K^bullet[1] is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules (proof lines 21282-21284).
Use the summands statement to conclude that K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules, finishing the proof (proof lines 21285-21287).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a complex K^bullet of R-modules and an integer m, and considers the R-algebra map R[x] -> R sending x to zero; it asserts that K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules if and only if it is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R[x]-modules (source lines 21258-21265). The proof first records that this is a special case of the pushforward pseudo-coherence statement, then gives a second, independent argument (proof lines 21268-21270). In the second argument, the exact sequence 0 -> R[x] -> R[x] -> R -> 0 shows that R is pseudo-coherent as an R[x]-module, so one implication follows from the pushforward statement (proof lines 21273-21276). For the other implication, assuming K^bullet is m-pseudo-coherent over R[x], the pullback statement gives that K^bullet tensor^L_{R[x]} R is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules; the pull-push statement then gives that K^bullet oplus K^bullet[1] is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules; and finally the summands statement gives that K^bullet itself is m-pseudo-coherent as a complex of R-modules (proof lines 21277-21287). The non-routine content is the reduction of the two-term base change complex to the direct sum K^bullet oplus K^bullet[1], which converts a question about a shift-and-sum into one about summands.
